contextual.summary: Nottingham makes a standard contextual offer (usually one grade lower) or an enhanced contextual offer (usually two grades lower) to Home students at UK non-fee-paying schools who meet one criterion; it's applied automatically from your UCAS form.
contextual.typicalReduction: Standard contextual: usually one grade lower; enhanced contextual: usually two grades lower (subject grades generally stay). Business School courses: standard contextual offer ABB.

criteria.detail: Live in an area with high levels of deprivation (University postcode checker) - standard offer
Refugee status from the Home Office - standard offer
Spent more than three months in care - standard offer
Completed a Sutton Trust post-16 programme not hosted by Nottingham (including Sutton Trust Online) - standard offer
Received free school meals on any census day in the 6 years up to the end of key stage 4 (verified via UCAS) - enhanced offer

Completed a Nottingham outreach programme: Sutton Trust Summer School at Nottingham, Sutton Trust Pathways to Medicine or Veterinary Medicine at Nottingham, Ambition 16-18 (Tier 1 / Tier 1+), or Realising Opportunities (Cohort 15 - 2024/25 and Cohort 16 - 2025/26 completers only) - enhanced offer

contextual.rulesText: You must have Home-UK fee status and your current or most recent school/college must be in the UK and not independent (fee-paying), except refugees and care leavers. 'One of the following must also apply' for a standard offer; for an enhanced offer 'You must also meet one of the following'. Young carers and disability are not contextual criteria.

source.evidence: To qualify for a standard contextual offer, you must have Home-UK fee status and your current or most recent school/college must be in the UK and cannot be an independent (fee-paying) school/college. ... One of the following must also apply:

programmes.name: Ambition Nottingham: 16-18
programmes.summary: A free two-year, mostly online programme for Year 12 students anywhere in the UK, with subject tasters, application advice and a VIP open day; Tier 1 members can get an enhanced contextual offer at Nottingham.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students (first term of Level 3 study: A levels, BTEC, IB or equivalent) from anywhere in the UK. Places are allocated to Tier 1 or Tier 2; only Tier 1 brings the offer and bursary benefits.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Tier 1 (needed for the enhanced contextual offer): UK Home fee status, a state-funded non-fee-paying school and GCSE English grade 4, plus one of: living in a high-deprivation area; free school meals in the 6 years up to the end of Year 11; or 'a number of' these: means-tested benefit or household income under £35,000, caring responsibilities, military family, disability, first generation, estranged. Gypsy/Roma/Traveller, refugee or care-experienced students also qualify (with discretion on school type and GCSEs). Tier 1 members must complete 8 live sessions.
benefits: Tier 1: enhanced contextual offer at Nottingham (usually two grades lower)
Tier 1: Nottingham Potential bursary if you enrol
Online subject tasters, Q&As with students, application and personal statement guidance
programmes.offerReduction: Enhanced contextual offer, usually two grades lower than the advertised entry requirements (Tier 1 / Tier 1+ only)

School of Economics courses don't require A-level Maths for Economics or PPE, but taking Maths lowers the offer from A*AA to AAA.

Business School courses (Industrial Economics, Finance Accounting and Management, Business and Management) are taught at Jubilee Campus in Nottingham, not University Park.

Young carers and disabled applicants aren't covered by contextual offers; Nottingham asks them to use its extenuating circumstances form instead.
